```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
```

Drug-specific validation vignettes (one per published model) are published on
the package website at
<https://nlmixr2.github.io/nlmixr2lib/articles/>. The **name** column links to
the vignette when one exists for that model. Models are grouped by their
location in `inst/modeldb/`: general PK/PD templates first, then specific drug
models, then models curated from the DDMoRe Foundation library.

```{r build-display, include = FALSE}
display <- nlmixr2lib::modeldb

# `label` and `category` are populated by buildModelDb() (see R/modeldb.R).
# Older modeldb dumps without these columns degrade gracefully -- derive on
# the fly using the same logic so an old data/modeldb.rda still renders.
if (!"label" %in% names(display)) {
  display$label <- vapply(display$filename, function(f) {
    base <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(f))
    parts <- strsplit(base, "_", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
    if (length(parts) >= 3 &&
        grepl("^[0-9]{4}[a-z]?$", parts[2]) &&
        parts[1] != "NA" && parts[2] != "NA") {
      drug <- paste(parts[-(1:2)], collapse = " ")
      drug <- paste0(toupper(substr(drug, 1, 1)), substr(drug, 2, nchar(drug)))
      sprintf("%s (%s %s)", drug, parts[1], parts[2])
    } else if (length(parts) >= 3 && parts[1] == "NA" && parts[2] == "NA") {
      sprintf("DDMoRe: %s", paste(parts[-(1:2)], collapse = " "))
    } else {
      gsub("_", " ", base, fixed = TRUE)
    }
  }, character(1))
}
if (!"category" %in% names(display)) {
  display$category <- ifelse(
    grepl("(^|/)specificDrugs/", display$filename), "specificDrugs",
    ifelse(grepl("(^|/)ddmore/", display$filename), "ddmore", "other")
  )
}

# `label` and `description` are PLAIN TEXT written by model authors, and both
# routinely contain characters that are markup in the two languages this table
# passes through:
#
#   * HTML -- `<` and `&` are common in descriptions ("toddlers <3 years",
#     "active->resting flux", "CLCR <= 40 mL/min", "<drug>" placeholders). Sent
#     to the browser unescaped, "<3 years" opens a tag and the rest of the cell
#     disappears.
#   * pandoc markdown -- the table is an HTML block inside a markdown document,
#     and pandoc's `markdown_in_html_blocks` extension (on by default) parses
#     the CONTENT of block-level HTML tags as markdown. That turns `_x_` and
#     `*x*` into emphasis (1600+ descriptions contain one or the other) and,
#     far worse, treats a `$` as opening inline math: a NONMEM description
#     mentioning `$PRED` or `$OMEGA` swallowed every row up to the next `$` on
#     the page and rendered ~1500 rows of the table as escaped source text.
#
# So the text is HTML-escaped here (keeping `escape = FALSE` in kable() for the
# deliberately-HTML `<a>` wrapper), and render_table() then emits the finished
# table as a pandoc RAW block so pandoc cannot reinterpret it. Both halves are
# needed: escaping alone leaves the markdown parsing, and a raw block alone
# leaves the browser eating "<3 years".
escapeHtml <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("&", "&amp;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("<", "&lt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub(">", "&gt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  gsub('"', "&quot;", x, fixed = TRUE)
}

# render_table() emits the table as a pandoc raw block, whose fence is closed
# by a line beginning with three backticks. Cell text is written inline after
# `<td ...>`, so it can only reach the start of a line if it contains a newline
# of its own. No shipped description does. Assert it rather than let a future
# one silently truncate the page -- the failure this vignette is being fixed
# for was exactly this shape, a stray character quietly eating the rest of the
# table, and it went unnoticed because nothing checked.
stopifnot(
  !any(grepl("\n", display$label, fixed = TRUE)),
  !any(grepl("\n", display$description, fixed = TRUE))
)

base_url <- "https://nlmixr2.github.io/nlmixr2lib/articles/"
display$label_html <- escapeHtml(display$label)
display$description_html <- escapeHtml(display$description)
display$name_html <- ifelse(
  is.na(display$vignette),
  display$label_html,
  sprintf('<a href="%s%s.html">%s</a>',
          base_url, escapeHtml(display$vignette), display$label_html)
)

# Map the internal category strings to the user-facing section labels.
display$section <- factor(
  display$category,
  levels = c("other", "specificDrugs", "ddmore"),
  labels = c("General", "Specific Drugs", "DDMoRe")
)

render_table <- function(rows) {
  rows <- rows[order(rows$label), , drop = FALSE]
  tbl <- rows[, c("name_html", "description_html")] |>
    stats::setNames(c("name", "description")) |>
    knitr::kable(
      format = "html",
      row.names = FALSE,
      table.attr = 'class="model-list-table"',
      escape = FALSE
    )
  # Raw block: hand the finished table to pandoc as-is (see the note above).
  knitr::raw_block(as.character(tbl), "html")
}
```

## General

```{r general, results = "asis", echo = FALSE}
render_table(subset(display, section == "General"))
```

## Specific Drugs

```{r specific, results = "asis", echo = FALSE}
render_table(subset(display, section == "Specific Drugs"))
```

## DDMoRe

```{r ddmore, results = "asis", echo = FALSE}
render_table(subset(display, section == "DDMoRe"))
```
